speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long you have had this lesion and if it started as a blister or an insect bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum

I see you have a significant history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and a recent flare of uveitis treated with steroids, which are all major risk factors for this condition. Given the rapid progression of the ulcer following the "ant bite" and your systemic autoimmune history, does the pain feel disproportionately severe compared to the size of the wound?
